```json
{
  "edition_title": "September 2026: The Doors Open Before the Deadlines Do",
  "edition_intro": "Ambitious young Nigerians do not wait for permission, they track deadlines like appointments. This edition rounds up five live opportunities worth your time this month: a fully funded master's in Beijing, a nine-figure naira startup grant, free tech expo access in Lagos, a ₦2.2 million essay prize, and a free route to a Microsoft certification. Move on these before the windows close.",
  "opportunities": [
    {
      "category": "scholarships",
      "title": "Schwarzman Scholars 2027-2028",
      "summary": "A fully funded one-year master's degree at Tsinghua University in Beijing, covering tuition, housing, travel, and a stipend, built for future global leaders under 30.",
      "deadline": "9 September 2026",
      "eligibility": "Bachelor's degree holders worldwide, generally aged 24 to 29; open to Nigerians and all nationalities; no GRE, GMAT, or Mandarin required",
      "apply_url": "https://www.schwarzmanscholars.org/admissions/application-instructions/",
      "body_md": "Schwarzman Scholars places roughly 150 young leaders a year at Tsinghua University for a one-year master's in Global Affairs, taught in English alongside students from China, the US, and beyond. The programme covers tuition, room and board, a laptop, course materials, travel, and a $4,000 personal stipend, and it deliberately recruits outside the usual Ivy League pipeline, which is why African applicants with strong leadership records stand a real shot.\n\nFounded by US private equity investor Stephen Schwarzman, the scholarship is run out of Tsinghua with an international board and is explicitly framed as training for people who will shape US-China and global relations over the next decades. For a Nigerian applicant, it is a rare, fully funded credential that opens doors in policy, finance, and technology circles most scholarships never touch, and unlike Rhodes or Chevening, it does not require a prior UK or US application to be in motion."
    },
    {
      "category": "grants",
      "title": "NiYA Startup Pitch 2.0",
      "summary": "Up to ₦100 million in non-dilutive funding for 100 Nigerian startups, plus mentorship and enterprise tools, through the federal government's youth platform.",
      "deadline": "Rolling",
      "eligibility": "Nigerian founders aged 18 to 35, with a startup that has at least two co-founders and a completed NiYA profile",
      "apply_url": "https://niya.gov.ng/",
      "body_md": "NiYA Startup Pitch 2.0 is the second round of the Nigerian Youth Academy's flagship funding challenge, backed by the Federal Ministry of Youth Development and launched from the Presidential Villa. It is selecting 100 startups to receive a share of ₦100 million in grant funding, alongside technical training and enterprise support designed to get very early founders investment ready rather than just cash rich.\n\nApplications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so unlike most government-linked grants there is no single cliff-edge deadline, but early, complete applications get first look. For a founder building outside Lagos or Abuja without an existing investor network, this is one of the few non-dilutive routes to capital that does not require years of revenue history first."
    },
    {
      "category": "conferences",
      "title": "GITEX Nigeria 2026",
      "summary": "Free registration for West Africa's largest tech expo and AI summit, putting young builders in the same room as global tech leaders and investors in Lagos.",
      "deadline": "3 September 2026",
      "eligibility": "Open to all; free visitor registration, no invitation required",
      "apply_url": "https://gitexnigeria.ng/",
      "body_md": "GITEX Nigeria runs from 31 August to 3 September 2026 across Abuja and Lagos, with the main Tech Expo and Future Economy Conference happening 2 to 3 September at the Lagos leg. It is the West African edition of the GITEX franchise, the same brand behind GITEX Global in Dubai, and it pulls in government leaders, telcos, cloud providers, and startup founders under one roof to talk AI, infrastructure, and the future economy.\n\nOrganizers have made general registration completely free for this edition, which is unusual for an expo of this scale. If you can get to Lagos in the next two days, walking the floor and sitting in on the AI Summit sessions is a low-cost way to meet people building the products you will compete or partner with next."
    },
    {
      "category": "conferences",
      "title": "Nigerian Economic Summit (NES #32)",
      "summary": "A two-day national dialogue on jobs and productivity in Abuja, putting young Nigerians in the same room as policymakers, investors, and business leaders shaping economic reform.",
      "deadline": "26 October 2026",
      "eligibility": "Open to the public via pre-registration; students, entrepreneurs, and young professionals attend alongside policymakers",
      "apply_url": "https://www.nesgroup.org/32",
      "body_md": "The Nigerian Economic Summit Group has run this annual summit for over three decades as the country's most influential private-sector-led policy dialogue. NES #32, themed 'Growth That Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity,' takes place 26 to 27 October 2026 at the Transcorp Hilton in Abuja, and pre-registration is open now.\n\nThis is not a startup pitch event, it is where the people who write Nigeria's economic policy sit across the table from the people affected by it. For a young Nigerian serious about influencing policy on jobs, tech regulation, or productivity rather than just reacting to it, getting a seat in the room is worth the trip to Abuja."
    },
    {
      "category": "competitions",
      "title": "NCDMB National Undergraduate Essay Competition 2026",
      "summary": "₦2.2 million in cash prizes and laptops for the best essays on local content and manufacturing, from Nigeria's oil and gas content regulator.",
      "deadline": "26 September 2026",
      "eligibility": "100 or 200 level students at Nigerian universities, polytechnics, or colleges of education",
      "apply_url": "https://ncdmbessay.ng/",
      "body_md": "Now in its tenth year, the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board's essay competition asks undergraduates to write on 'Promoting Manufacturing for Sustainable Local Content Development,' a topic tied directly to NCDMB's mandate of keeping oil and gas value where Nigerians can capture it. Winners split ₦2.2 million in cash, the top ten national finalists each get a laptop, and the winning essay gets published in the Board's Local Content Digest.\n\nIt costs nothing to enter beyond the essay itself, and it rewards clear thinking over connections or capital, which makes it one of the more accessible national competitions on this list. First and second year students who can write persuasively about industrial policy have a real shot at a prize most of their peers will never hear about in time to enter."
    },
    {
      "category": "certifications",
      "title": "Digital Skills Nigeria Free Microsoft Certification Vouchers",
      "summary": "Free Microsoft Learn training plus a fully paid certification exam voucher in Azure, Power BI, AI, or security, once you pass the qualifying mock exam.",
      "deadline": "Rolling (score 60%+ on the course mock exam by the 27th of any month)",
      "eligibility": "Nigerian citizens aged 16 to 35",
      "apply_url": "https://www.digitalskillsnigeria.org/",
      "body_md": "Digital Skills Nigeria is a partnership between the Federal Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy and Microsoft, offering free access to advanced courses including Azure Data Scientist, Azure Security Engineer, Azure Administrator, Power BI Data Analyst, and Azure AI Fundamentals. Complete the course, score above 60% on the mock exam before the 27th of the month, and you are added to a qualified candidates list that unlocks a free certification exam voucher.\n\nThis runs every month rather than on a single annual cycle, so there is no long wait for the next intake, and it is a direct, no-cost path to an internationally recognized Microsoft credential that Nigerian employers actively screen for. For anyone building toward a cloud or data career without the money for a $165 exam fee, this removes the single biggest cost barrier."
    }
  ]
}
```
